text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday.
- Workers of Croatian railways (HZ) announce a new strike after 20 days of stoppage. The company management threatenes to demand compensation for losses and sack the organisers.
- Japan and South Korea to back Croatia's admittance to the World Trade Organisation, foreign minister Mate Granic said during a recent visit.

- Croatia negotiates investment in the construction of a 120 km-long stretch of future highway linking capital with the main port in Split with a U.S. company Bechtel. Investor may be granted a 20 year concession.
- Foreign companies seem more and more interested in financing construction of power plants in Croatia.
- State health service suffers from a chronic cash shortage, its director Stjepan Turek says. Its' budget to rise some 10 percent next year.
- Croatia's Air Force may buy up to 12 F-16C figher jets.
- Deputy PM Borislav Skegro foresees a strong investment growth in 1997 and says problem of insolvency should soon be resolved.
- The Sabor passes a social programme according to which Croatia to spend 6.7 billion kuna on welfare next year. -
Bread and milk should be exempt from profit taxation, Mate Perkovic, head of the tax board says. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
